Hi Tessa,

We're preparing our vendor review ahead of a quarterly audit and need a current subprocessor inventory and a succinct description of any data transfers originating from Redwood that land in India (including backups, analytics, or any third-party support access).

Specific asks:
- Full roster of subprocessors (name / primary function / country) engaged in production or logging.
- Which subprocessors have potential to receive personal data from EU or US customers and the legal basis for transfer (SCCs, adequacy decisions, or other).
- Any subcontractors or temporary vendors (e.g., support contractors) with access to customer data, and whether they operate in India.
- A short note on retention policies for logs/backups and where they are stored.

Can you get this to us by tomorrow EOD? If you need more time, let me know what you can provide this week.

Thanks,
Paul

Paul —

Attached is the current subprocessor inventory and a one-slide dataflow summary for EdgeWave's review. High-level points up front:

- Roster highlights (attached PDF contains full table):
  • Data storage: AtlasCloud LLC (US, primary storage, encrypted at rest)
  • CDN/edge: NorthPoint CDN (US/EU) — no India PoPs for customer data; cache purging only
  • Log processing: LogFlow Ltd (EU) — analytics; pseudonymized by default
  • Operational support (limited access): SupportWorks (India) — incident response only; access via bastion with MFA and recorded sessions
  • KMS/HSM: KeySafe Partners (US) — customer keys managed, HSM-backed

- Transfers and legal safeguards:
  • Where EU data is routed to non-EEA subprocessors we rely on standard contractual clauses (SCCs) and updated EU addendum language as appropriate.
  • For US -> India operational access (SupportWorks) we rely on contractual controls, access minimization, and SOC2 controls; SupportWorks is on our onboarding checklist and undergoes quarterly access reviews.

- Backups & retention:
  • Backups for customer data are encrypted and stored in US/EU regions only. Internal operational snapshots for debugging (redacted) may be available to SupportWorks in India for limited durations (<=72 hours) and are explicitly listed in the attached roster.

- Evidence and audits:
  • We can provide SOC2 report excerpts and our onboarding questionnaire answers (redacted PII) under NDA.
  • If EdgeWave needs a signed DPA addendum with explicit subprocessor clauses, I've attached a DocuSign link to a standard addendum we use; Marissa will coordinate contract redlines.

Related links:
- Subprocessor PDF: https://drive.redwood.ai/shared/EdgeWave/subprocessors/subprocessor_inventory_20280216.pdf
- DPA addendum (DocuSign): https://app.docusign.com/documents/abc123-edgewave-dpa-addendum
- HubSpot record: HUBSPOT-Contact-104859

If you want, I can provide a short spreadsheet mapping each subprocessor to the specific categories of data they may touch (PII, logs, metrics). Let me know which format helps your audit team.

Thanks —
Tessa

Tessa —

Received the packet, thanks for the quick turnaround. A couple of follow-ups after a quick internal review:
- Can you confirm that no customer-production backups are retained in India? The paragraph about operational snapshots sounds like the only potential exception; we need explicit confirmation of geolocation for full backups.
- For SupportWorks (India) please confirm whether any employees have standing access to decrypted data, or whether access requires a live justification and is session-recorded (we prefer session-only with recorded sessions).
- Legal is asking for the latest SOC2 report and the onboarding questionnaire mentioned; we've sent an NDA to Marissa's inbox.

If you can confirm the two technical points above and drop the SOC2 to Marissa, we should be able to close this item.

Paul
